_comment: Curated catalogue of real market data vendors, searched offline with no key and no network. Ability 17's first layer. Prices and coverage change -- verify on the vendor's own page before relying on a number here. This is a map of where to look, not a price list.

sources.name: Binance
sources.notes: Already wired in. Public klines carry taker-buy volume, so real delta is available without paying. This is what makes the free demo possible.

sources.name: Databento
sources.cost: pay per GB, tick data is the expensive part
sources.notes: Already wired in. The only source here with true MBO/MBP order flow for futures. Tick data is one to three orders of magnitude dearer than bars -- the cost notifier says so before every pull.

sources.name: Polygon.io
sources.notes: Already wired in. Best value for US equities and forex minute history.

sources.name: yfinance
sources.history: daily back decades; 1-minute only the last ~7 days
sources.notes: Already wired in as the free fallback. Unofficial endpoint: it breaks periodically and the 7-day intraday limit is real. Fine for a look, not for a year of minute bars.

sources.name: Dukascopy
sources.notes: Free tick-level FX going back two decades. Download the file and `ee-agent data ingest` reads it -- the schema is inferred, you do not have to describe it.

sources.name: HistData
sources.notes: Free 1-minute and tick FX by month. Bid/ask only, no volume -- the flow layer degrades to proxies and says so.

sources.name: FirstRate Data
sources.notes: Buy once, own the file. Good when you want a fixed historical set rather than a subscription.

sources.name: Kibot
sources.notes: Long histories, unadjusted and adjusted variants. Check which you are buying -- the integrity engine will back-adjust splits for you either way.

sources.name: Tiingo
sources.notes: Cheap and reliable for daily equity history. Not yet wired in -- ingest a CSV, or ask me to add a fetcher.

sources.name: Alpaca
sources.cost: free tier with IEX data, about $99/month for full SIP
sources.notes: The free tier is IEX-only, which is a thin slice of true volume. Fine for shape, wrong for volume-sensitive strategies.

sources.name: Nasdaq Data Link
sources.notes: Formerly Quandl. Strong for commodities and macro series, daily only. Good for regime context, not for intraday execution.

sources.name: Kaiko
sources.notes: Institutional crypto with real order book depth. Overkill unless you are trading size; Binance public data is free and carries delta.

sources.name: Tardis.dev
sources.notes: Full L2/L3 crypto order book replay. The right answer if your strategy genuinely reads the book rather than bars.

sources.name: Barchart
sources.notes: Broad coverage including agricultural and energy futures that other vendors skip.

sources.name: Interactive Brokers
sources.cost: free with a funded account plus exchange data fees
sources.notes: If you already have an IBKR account this is effectively free. Pacing limits make bulk history slow -- fine for topping up, painful for a first pull.

sources.name: CME DataMine
sources.history: back to the 1970s on some contracts
sources.notes: Straight from the exchange, so it is the reference other vendors are checked against. Expensive and delivered as bulk files.
